decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 3 addresses are shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — j.sandy.flacke@maine.gov → J.Sandy.Flacke@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 5 email addresses sit in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Let a short row of cards reach the page edge
decisions.why: 1 row holds cards in columns that add up to less than the full twelve, so the grid stops short and the rest of the line is blank. The cards are narrower than they need to be, which makes everything inside them taller — and the page longer. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.
